office_does: The assessor sets the market value of every taxable property in Kitsap County and runs appeals and the senior, disabled and other exemption programs; the office does not set tax rates.
race_blurb: Incumbent Phil Cook (Prefers Republican Party), assessor since 2015, runs on office efficiency and a nationally recognized exemption workflow. Navy veteran and Redfin agent Michael Simonds (Prefers Democratic Party) says high-value properties are under-assessed relative to working-class neighborhoods and wants data-driven modernization.

candidates.summary: Kitsap County Assessor since 2015, with a background in real estate, mortgage lending and property management, running on accuracy, transparency and efficiency.
highlights: Assessor since 2015; nearly 25 years in Kitsap real estate and property management [S1]
Says the office handled a 76% jump in senior/disabled exemption applications without added staff or funding [S3]
Says the exemption workflow won national recognition and became a state-recommended practice [S1][S3]
Says tax rates are set by taxing districts and levies, not the assessor [S3]

experience.basis: Three-term incumbent (since 2015) running on the office's operational record.

spending.basis: Stresses fiscal responsibility and absorbing added workload through process improvement 'without additional staff or taxpayer funding.'

candidates.summary: Navy veteran and Redfin real-estate agent who has not held office, proposing data analytics to correct neighborhood-level valuation imbalances.
highlights: Former Navy nuclear missile technician; Redfin's first Kitsap-based agent since 2017 [S1]
Says working-class neighborhoods often pay more than their share while high-value properties lag [S1]
Proposes online valuation and appeal tools and outreach on exemptions for seniors, veterans, disabled and lower-income residents [S1]

experience.basis: First-time candidate running on 'accountability, transparency, and modernization' against a 12-year incumbent.
